attacks.claim: The weekly public CC-BY open-data export publishes ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking, verified, and created_at per response. For small wards or zips, these quasi-identifiers can re-identify individual residents, and a public CC-BY release cannot be recalled. No k-anonymity threshold, suppression, or aggregation step is specified; removing resident_id is the only de-identification.
attacks.evidence: "one CSV per poll on data.ourtown.org with columns ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking, verified, created_at. resident_id is removed before export."

attacks.claim: Verified residents' address, zip, birth_year, and gender were collected for jury-pool demographic balance reports, not for public release. Feeding them into a public export is a purpose change with no stated consent, notice, or purpose-limitation review. It also conflicts with the agreed anonymous-first, optional-verification constraint.
attacks.evidence: "Verified residents already have address, zip, birth_year, gender (collected at optional verification for the jury-pool-style demographic balance reports)."

attacks.claim: Linkability: verified rows carry ward, zip, birth_year, gender, and verified=true alongside created_at, so responses can be joined across polls and weekly exports to build individual participation and demographic profiles. Removing resident_id does not prevent this.
attacks.evidence: "resident_id is removed before export."

attacks.claim: The plan sends automated SMS to about 142,000 registered voters from a purchased county voter file with no evidence of prior consent. This raises TCPA exposure for automated texts to mobile numbers, Twilio/carrier messaging-policy problems for unsolicited traffic, and possible state restrictions on voter-file use outside election or government purposes. No legal or consent review step exists.
attacks.evidence: "Purchase the county voter registration file from the County Clerk ($400, includes mobile numbers where provided). Load numbers into Twilio and send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000)"

attacks.claim: The SMS blast is a one-way, irreversible external action with no pilot, approval gate, or rollback before the send. Recipients cannot be unsent, and the 3 automated reminders extend the exposure over 10 days.
attacks.evidence: "send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000) with a link to the first poll, then 3 automated reminders over 10 days."

attacks.claim: The core justification is contradicted by the artifact's own survey: only 9% of 1,240 respondents want polls, while the top request (61%, see how council members voted and why) is absent from the plan. Polls are nonetheless declared the centerpiece with no demand evidence.
attacks.evidence: "Polls on upcoming items — 9%" versus "Ward Voice ... is the centerpiece of the FY27 roadmap."

attacks.claim: Unverified responses are accepted with self-selected ward, and the per-device-fingerprint limit is trivially bypassed. Only IP traffic over 3/min is queued, and queued items are not explicitly excluded from tallies. Fabricated responses can dominate the all-responses column and the public export, which publishes that column as sentiment.
attacks.evidence: "Unverified responses are accepted; ward is self-selected for unverified users" and "1 response per poll per device fingerprint + 1 per verified resident; unverified responses over 3/min from one IP are queued for review."

attacks.claim: Staff receive the full CSV containing birth_year, gender, and zip, but no authorization model, export scoping, or audit trail is specified for this sensitive data.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authz model for staff export access and audit trail; "Council staff have the same CSV plus a PDF summary emailed Monday 07:00"

attacks.claim: Device fingerprints and IP addresses are stored for rate limiting, but the plan states no retention period, hashing, or exclusion from exports and staff CSVs. This conflicts with the anonymous-first constraint.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention period and fingerprint/IP handling in exports; "1 response per poll per device fingerprint"

attacks.claim: Instant-runoff behavior is undefined: exhausted ballots, partial rankings, tie-breaking, and handling of rankings that reference options no longer present are unspecified. Per-ward IRV is named but not defined as a method.
attacks.evidence: "results are shown per ward with instant-runoff tallies" and "poll options are frozen once the first response arrives"

attacks.claim: Resubmission semantics are unspecified (edit, overwrite, or reject). With staff unable to edit or delete, a mis-click or abuse is permanent, and the plan gives no correction path for residents.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: resubmission/correction behavior; "Staff cannot edit or delete responses"

attacks.claim: No path exists to remove spam, harassing or mis-authored polls, or polls attached to the wrong agenda item. Immutable options and responses leave ops without a remediation route.
attacks.evidence: "Staff cannot edit or delete responses; poll options are frozen once the first response arrives."

attacks.claim: The SMS blast and its reminders will create a traffic spike at first-poll launch on self-hosted servers. The week-5 load test targets 5k concurrency without modeling texted-link spikes, and there is no capacity fallback.
attacks.evidence: "load test (target 5k concurrent), launch" and "send an automated SMS to every registered voter in the city (~142,000) with a link to the first poll"

attacks.claim: The review queue for over-limit unverified responses has no capacity, SLA, or alerting, and staff review time is not in the 5-week plan. A brigade can fill the queue.
attacks.evidence: "unverified responses over 3/min from one IP are queued for review."

attacks.claim: The outreach pipeline depends on a single third-party provider (Twilio) for delivery and opt-out, with no alternative path, creating lock-in and a single point of failure for opt-out handling.
attacks.evidence: "Load numbers into Twilio ... Reply STOP handled by Twilio's default opt-out."

attacks.claim: The poll is presented as a direct voice on items council is deciding, timed before budget hearings, with no analysis of election, lobbying, or public-advocacy rules that could apply to a nonprofit's poll used in official contexts.
attacks.evidence: "Ward Voice gives residents a direct voice on the items council is actually deciding" and "Target launch: before the FY27 budget hearings"

attacks.claim: Success metrics measure response volume and new-user share, not participation quality or any link to council deliberation, which is the stated mission.
attacks.evidence: "6,000 poll responses in the first 30 days." ABSENT: any metric linking results to council action.

attacks.claim: Drag-based ranking is specified without keyboard or screen-reader alternatives, and accessibility is deferred to a single week-5 pass before launch.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: resident ranking UI (mobile-first, drag or tap-to-rank)" and "Week 5: accessibility pass, load test"

attacks.claim: Five weeks for two backend engineers covering poll authoring, IRV, open-data export, PDF, voter-file import, and an SMS pipeline is not credible, and the scope has drifted beyond the survey-backed need.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: open-data export, staff PDF, voter-file import + SMS pipeline"

attacks.claim: The 6,000-response and 30%-new-user targets and the 5k-concurrency target have no stated baseline or derivation from traffic data, against a base of ~18,000 users.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: basis for "6,000 poll responses in the first 30 days" and "target 5k concurrent"; base population is ~18,000 users.

attacks.claim: Ward derivation has two code paths with no rule for a verified resident who self-selects a different ward than their address implies.
attacks.evidence: "ward is self-selected for unverified users and derived from address for verified users"

attacks.claim: No plain-language IRV explainer is included in the ranking UI, so residents may misunderstand how their ranking is tallied.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: IRV explainer or onboarding copy in Week 2 resident ranking UI.

attacks.claim: The split 'verified' and 'all responses' columns have no explanation, so residents may misread the difference.
attacks.evidence: "split into 'verified' and 'all responses' columns"

attacks.claim: Twilio SMS cost is unbudgeted: roughly 568,000 segments at 142,000 recipients times 4 messages, before carrier fees.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: Twilio cost estimate or budget cap

attacks.claim: No alerting or failure handling is described for the Monday staff PDF or the weekly open-data export, including partial publication.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: failure handling and alerting for "Open-data export (weekly, public, CC-BY)"
